changelog: 1.0.0 — première version : usage québécois (OQLF), glossaire des termes choisis, passages douteux signalés ; pas une traduction certifiée.

inputs.prompt: Build the firm's FR/EN terminology from these documents: {{inputs.documents}}. Existing glossary to extend, if any: {{inputs.glossary}}. Output a table: English term | French term (Québec usage) | Source of the term | Note. One row per recurring term; keep existing rows as they are unless they contradict the documents, in which case flag it. Output the table in the plain form « English | French | Source | Note », one row per line, so it can be pasted into the other Studios. The first line of your answer is exactly this sentence: fr « Traduction automatisée non certifiée — à faire réviser par un professionnel avant tout usage, surtout pour un document juridique. » en « Automated, uncertified translation — to be reviewed by a professional before any use, above all for a legal document. » (use the one that matches the output language). Mark anything you are unsure of as « À réviser » (fr) or « To review » (en). Name the terminology source of every term you choose (the usage recommended by the Office québécois de la langue française, OQLF, and its Grand dictionnaire terminologique, when one applies; otherwise say « usage courant »). Never invent a legal term: when no established Québec term exists, keep the source term in brackets and flag the passage. Never quote a statute; refer to it by name only.
